interpretation.endpoint_path_agreement: 40 randomized datasets; max endpoint difference below 5e-13 and zero threshold-decision mismatches in 400 random threshold checks.
interpretation.query_work: V3 used about 9.95% of V2 _stats calls in this local prototype comparison.
interpretation.runtime_scope: Local Python timing only; not a deployment-performance claim.
interpretation.independent_reference: For 1000 small random cases, a direct descending endpoint-event sweep solved the same piecewise-linear water-filling root independently. V3 was not worse than V2 in all 1000 cases and had smaller maximum absolute log_d error.

algorithmic_guard: Cache is cleared on every append; no root bracket is reused across envelope changes.
Cached neighboring m values contribute only sign-certified c-bounds; they do not change the target or statistical denominator.
Every iteration retains an ordinary midpoint bracket update, so progress is guaranteed even if the piecewise-linear jump is rejected.
Early jump acceptance requires a stricter residual tolerance than the public fail-closed residual check.
The final width target matches V2's 40-step global c-resolution or improves it from a narrower warm bracket.
This is a computational refactor only; predictable-weight and e-process assumptions are unchanged.
scope: Synthetic/randomized local validation, not production latency.
No claim of bit-for-bit equality with V2 internal floating-point paths; the decision-relevant endpoints agreed to <5e-13 in the tested suite.
The independent event sweep was used only on small n validation cases and is not the streaming implementation.
